headline: Figma Adds New Tools to Help AI Assistants Design Better

levels.label: Grade 3-4
levels.summary: Figma is a computer program that helps people design things like apps and websites. Figma just added new tools to help computer helpers, called AI agents, do a better job when they help design things. One new tool is called Figma Specs. It lets teams write down simple rules about how their designs should look, like what colors or shapes to use. This way, when an AI agent helps make something, it follows the same rules as the humans. Figma also made a tool called code layers available to more people. This tool turns designs into real computer code, so people can test how an app might actually work. Someone can even ask the AI to change parts of the code to try new ideas. Figma also connected with a tool called Payload, which helps manage words and pictures on websites. These changes matter because many companies now use AI to help build apps and websites faster. Figma wants to make sure AI still follows the rules humans set, so designs look neat and work well. Figma also shared that India is one of its biggest groups of users outside the United States.

levels.label: Grade 5-6
levels.summary: Figma, a popular design software company, announced several new features to help both humans and AI assistants work better together when designing apps and websites. One major tool is called Figma Specs. It works like a simple notebook where design teams can write out their rules, such as preferred colors, fonts, or layouts. This notebook can be viewed alongside actual designs, and AI tools can check it to make sure their work matches a company's style. This matters because AI can sometimes act unpredictably, so giving it clear rules helps keep designs consistent. Figma also expanded a feature called code layers, which lets designers turn their visual designs directly into working code. This means a website or app idea can quickly become something real that people can actually click through and test, instead of just looking like a picture. Users can even ask an AI assistant to change the code to try new design ideas. Figma explained that although way more code is being written today thanks to AI, most of it is used to experiment with design ideas rather than to launch final products. Figma also connected its tools with Payload, a content management system it bought last year, to help people build and manage website content more easily. These updates show how design and computer programming are becoming more blended, especially as AI becomes a bigger part of the creative process. Figma highlighted that India is now one of its largest markets outside the United States, showing how these tools affect designers around the world, not just in the U.S.

levels.label: Grade 7-8
levels.summary: Figma, a major design software company used by companies worldwide, introduced several new tools aimed at helping both people and artificial intelligence work together more effectively when building digital designs. The centerpiece feature, called Figma Specs, allows design teams to write out their company's visual rules, such as specific colors, fonts, or layout styles, in a simple text format. This 'rulebook' can be referenced by both human designers and AI tools, ensuring that anything created, whether by a person or an algorithm, stays consistent with a brand's intended look. This matters because AI systems don't always produce predictable results, so having clear guidelines helps companies maintain quality control even as they begin relying more on automated design help. Figma also expanded access to its 'code layers' feature, which converts visual designs directly into working code, allowing teams to test interactive prototypes rather than static pictures. Users can also instruct AI tools to tweak this code to quickly try out different design options. According to Figma's chief design officer, this reflects a larger shift happening in the tech industry: AI has caused a huge increase in the amount of code being written, but most of this code isn't meant for final products. Instead, it's used to explore and discover what a product should even look like before it's finalized. In addition, Figma integrated its design tools with Payload, a content management platform it acquired last year, making it easier for teams to create websites and manage their content without needing separate systems. Figma also announced partnerships with more than 20 new AI tools that can plug directly into its platform. These updates highlight how deeply AI is becoming embedded in creative work, not just as a novelty, but as a core part of professional design workflows. The event where these updates were announced took place in India, which Figma says is now its largest market outside the United States, showing how influential these design tools have become on a global scale, including in fast-growing tech industries.

levels.label: Grade 9-10
levels.summary: At its first Config event held in India, design software company Figma unveiled a set of new features intended to help both human designers and AI-powered assistants collaborate more effectively while adhering to consistent design standards. Central to this announcement is a new tool called Figma Specs, a markdown-based editor that allows teams to document their design language, including rules about colors, typography, and layout, in a clear, structured way. This document can function as a standalone reference or be embedded directly within a design file, and it can even incorporate diagrams, code snippets, and other design elements. The purpose is to give both human teams and AI agents a shared reference point, ensuring that as AI becomes more involved in the design process, its output still aligns with a brand's established visual identity. This is particularly significant because AI-generated content can be unpredictable, or as the article describes it, 'non-deterministic,' meaning the same prompt might not always produce the same result. By creating a centralized system of design rules, Figma aims to reduce this unpredictability and give companies more control over AI-assisted design work. Alongside this, Figma expanded public access to its 'code layers' feature, which transforms visual designs into functional code, enabling more interactive prototypes rather than static mockups. This feature, first introduced in a private beta, allows users to instruct AI agents to generate code from a design or revise existing code to experiment with new ideas. According to Figma's chief design officer, Loredana Crisan, this reflects a broader industry trend: AI has dramatically increased the volume of code being written, but most of it isn't intended for final products. Instead, it's used as a tool for discovery, helping teams figure out what a product should look and function like before committing to a final build. Figma also integrated Payload, a headless content management system it acquired last year, into its Figma Make product, streamlining how teams generate websites and manage content. The company reported that Payload's usage has grown sixfold over the past year. Additionally, Figma announced that its platform now connects with more than 20 new AI tools through its Model Context Protocol, including several AI products developed specifically in India. This reflects Figma's broader strategic push into the Indian market, where it recently opened its first office and says it now counts 40% of India's top 100 publicly listed companies among its users, underscoring how significant this market has become for the company's global growth.

levels.label: Grade 11+
levels.summary: During its first Config event held in India, design platform Figma unveiled a suite of new features designed to formalize how both human teams and AI-driven design agents operate within its ecosystem, reflecting a broader industry effort to make AI-assisted creative work more reliable and brand-consistent. The centerpiece of this announcement is Figma Specs, a markdown-based editor that enables companies to document their design language, encompassing rules around color schemes, typography, and layout conventions, in a structured, easily referenced format. This specification document can exist independently or be integrated directly into the design canvas, and it supports embedding other Figma elements such as FigJam diagrams, code snippets, and existing designs. The underlying goal is to establish a centralized source of truth that both human designers and AI agents can consult, ensuring that AI-generated contributions remain faithful to a brand's established visual identity. This development is particularly significant given the inherently unpredictable, or 'non-deterministic,' nature of AI systems, which can produce varying outputs even from similar prompts. By codifying design rules into an accessible reference system, Figma is attempting to introduce a layer of predictability and governance into AI-assisted workflows, a growing concern as companies increasingly rely on AI to accelerate design and development processes. Complementing this, Figma expanded public access to its 'code layers' feature, which converts static visual designs into functional code, enabling teams to build more interactive, testable prototypes rather than relying solely on static mockups. Originally introduced in private beta, this feature now allows users to instruct AI agents to generate or modify code directly from a design, streamlining the iterative design-to-development pipeline. Figma's chief design officer, Loredana Crisan, contextualized this shift by noting that while AI has caused a seventeen-fold increase in the volume of code being produced, software release rates have only grown by a factor of 1.3, suggesting that much of this AI-generated code serves an exploratory function, helping teams prototype and discover product direction rather than ship finalized products. Figma also announced the integration of Payload, a headless content management system it acquired last year, into its Figma Make product, enabling more seamless website generation and content management; the company reported that Payload's adoption has increased sixfold over the past twelve months. Additionally, Figma's platform now supports connections with more than 20 new AI tools through its Model Context Protocol, including international products like Grok Bot and Dia, as well as Sarvam, an AI startup based in India. This expansion aligns with Figma's strategic investment in the Indian market, where the company opened its first office last year and now reports that 40% of India's top 100 publicly traded companies use its platform, positioning India as Figma's largest market outside the United States and underscoring the global stakes involved in shaping how AI integrates into professional design and software development workflows.

questions: If you were designing an app with the help of an AI assistant, what rules would you want to give it to make sure it followed your vision?
How do you think tools that let AI write and change code might change what jobs or skills will be important in the future?
Why might it be important for companies to make sure AI-generated designs or code still match human rules and expectations, rather than letting AI do whatever it wants?
